core_ideas.idea: One AI design tool can replace a patchwork of apps for graphics
core_ideas.why: Kittl bundles AI generation, customizable templates, text effects, and mockups so you don't jump between Canva, Photoshop and mockup generators
core_ideas.trade_off: You still need to learn a new interface and AI can make designs look generic if you don't customize them

core_ideas.idea: You can now edit video by typing prompts instead of dragging on a timeline
core_ideas.why: 13 tools in one list and 12 in another let you type chat commands for cuts, silence removal and refinements instead of learning DaVinci, iMovie or CapCut
core_ideas.trade_off: Prompt editing is faster for beginners but gives less frame-perfect control than manual timeline editing

core_ideas.idea: New editing primitives like avatar cloning, text-to-video and transcript editing are the building blocks
core_ideas.why: Instead of just trimming clips, you can generate an avatar presenter, turn text into video, or edit by editing the transcript
core_ideas.trade_off: Avatars and auto-generated footage can feel less authentic and may need disclosure or extra polishing

core_ideas.idea: The first 3 seconds win or lose the viewer, so use ready-made hook templates
core_ideas.why: 50 fill-in-the-blank storytelling hooks are designed to stop scrolling and boost engagement on Instagram and short-form video
core_ideas.trade_off: Hooks only work if the rest of the story delivers; clickbaity openers hurt trust if you don't follow through

core_ideas.idea: Storytelling is a learnable system you can improve in minutes, not just talent
core_ideas.why: The 9-minute guide breaks engaging storytelling into practical tips you can apply to any video or post right away
core_ideas.trade_off: Quick tips give you a start but still need practice and feedback to sound natural on camera

connections.reason: Both curate the same 12-13 AI video editors that replace DaVinci/iMovie/CapCut with typing
Both show AI replacing traditional creative software — Kittl for design, chat tools for video editing
Kittl shows all-in-one design control while Veo 3 comparison shows JSON vs natural prompts for precise video control
Both turn text prompts into video — one edits existing footage by chatting, one generates seamless transitions in Veo 3
Typing to edit video extends to typing JSON to direct cinematic style, lighting and cuts in Veo 3
Hooks get attention in 3 seconds, the 9-minute framework keeps people watching after the hook
When AI handles tedious cuts and auto-edits, you free up time to focus on story structure
A strong fill-in-the-blank hook plus precise Veo 3 prompting turns a concept into a finished viral clip fast

gaps.missing: how to distribute and market after creation — thumbnails, posting times, algorithms, and analytics
gaps.why_it_matters: Hooks and edits get views only if people see the content; you need a system to test what actually performs

gaps.missing: hands-on workflow, pricing and limits for Kittl and the 12-13 AI video editors
gaps.why_it_matters: Beginners need to know what’s free, what watermarks, and which tool to pick first without overwhelm

gaps.missing: audio, voiceover and music for AI video — cleanup, captions, and licensing
gaps.why_it_matters: Sound is half of retention and many AI editors upsell voice and music features

gaps.missing: copyright, disclosure and brand consistency when using AI avatars and generated designs
gaps.why_it_matters: Using avatars and AI mockups at scale can create trust and legal issues if not handled transparently

learning_order.why_here: Foundation: understand what makes any story engaging in under 9 minutes
Apply story to the opening — practice 50 hook templates to stop the scroll in 3 seconds
Create visuals to support your story — learn Kittl for thumbnails, templates and mockups
Learn the new way to edit — overview of 13 prompt-based tools that replace timeline editing
Go deeper on the same idea with 12 typed-editing tools for avatars, transcript cuts and auto-refinements
